title: Bridge Closure in Ring Topology
description: This scenario explores bridge closure dynamics within a ring communication topology. The disturbance creates coordination challenges that test the agents' ability to adapt, communicate effectively, and maintain freight flow under adverse conditions.
edge_cases_to_watch: Freight must be rerouted through longer path
Agents at east depot may become isolated due to communication bottleneck
Capacity saturation on the north-south route due to massive rerouting
Information propagation delay in ring topology prevents rapid consensus on reroute
Conflicting agent decisions causing deadlocks at capacity-limited nodes
coordination_challenges: Latency in consensus: Agents must propagate the bridge closure status through the ring to reach all nodes
Resource competition: Multiple agents attempting to use the low-capacity 'east-north' route simultaneously
Priority-based preemption: High-priority agents must signal others to yield capacity on the alternate route
Information asymmetry: Agents on the far side of the ring acting on stale routing data
suggested_agent_strategies: Distributed Consensus: Use ring-passing to synchronize the 'bridge-closed' state across all agents
Dynamic Re-routing: Pre-calculate secondary paths (e.g., east -> north -> south) upon status updates
Congestion Awareness: Monitor route utilization and switch to secondary paths before capacity is reached
Priority Signaling: High-priority agents broadcast 'reservation' requests to mitigate collision at bottleneck nodes

coordination_challenges: Freight must be rerouted through longer path

success_criteria: Agents adapt communication to topology constraints
Recovery from disruption within expected turns
Minimal capacity violations on alternative routes
